subject: Accelerator Holdback & Committed Wallet Drawdown — terms and true-up
messages:
From: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vectorai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Alex Wang <alex.wang@vectorai.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing chat — committed spend structure

Grace — thanks for the call earlier. VectorAI is evaluating a two-year commitment but we have two main constraints: (1) we need a predictable monthly burn for budgeting, and (2) we want downside protection in year 1 if usage ramps slower than expected.

A few concrete asks from our finance team:
- Can Redwood structure a committed wallet that draws down monthly but returns an unused holdback to us at each 6-month true-up if we are below ramp targets?
- Term discount: can we get a steeper rate at 24 months vs 12 months (we're thinking 15% vs 8%)?
- Any minimums or accelerator clauses that increase billed usage if we exceed thresholds?

We can share a simple ramp profile (month-by-month expected tokens) if that helps.

Thanks,
Lisa
Head of Finance, VectorAI
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vectorai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Initial pricing chat — committed spend structure

Lisa — appreciate the clarity and the ramp offer, that helps a lot. High-level responses below, and Ben + Karthik are on the thread to align on the commercial and operational details.

- Committed wallet with monthly drawdown + 6-month true-up: yes, we can do that. The typical approach we recommend is a monthly drawdown cadence with a biannual reconciliation window where unused credits can be either (a) returned as a cash credit to VectorAI, or (b) converted to a discounted overage buffer (we commonly lock at 70% refund + 30% retained as buffer). We can be flexible on the split for enterprise deals.

- Term discounts: 8% for 12 months vs 15% for 24 months is in the ballpark. The discount can be layered: base term discount + a ramp attainment accelerator that unlocks additional discounts once your realized run-rate hits pre-agreed milestones.

- Accelerator / earnings: our standard accelerator increases the committed baseline for billing only (not retroactive) when monthly usage surpasses the committed monthly target by >40% for two consecutive months. We can also structure a corridor (e.g., partial accelerator between 20-40%).

Next steps: Ben will draft a proposal with two options (12m / 24m) showing line-by-line economics and three ramp scenarios (conservative/expected/upside). Karthik will outline the operational terms for the 6-month true-up and reporting requirements. Can you share the month-by-month ramp profile you mentioned by EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Grace
Director, Enterprise GTM — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vectorai.com>, Alex Wang <alex.wang@vectorai.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: RDW-4521 — draft economics and holdback options

Team — attaching a draft summary (see attachments). Key points from the pricing model:
- Option A (12 months): $600k committed wallet, 8% term discount, monthly drawdown = $50k baseline. 6-month true-up: refund policy = 60% cash refund of remaining wallet, 40% retained as prepay buffer to cover overage risk.
- Option B (24 months): $1.1M committed wallet, 15% term discount, monthly drawdown = frontloaded schedule (first 3 months at 60% of baseline to support ramp) then normalized. 6-month true-up: 70% cash refund, 30% buffer.
- Accelerator: for either option, if monthly usage > baseline x 1.4 for two consecutive months, that month’s billing converts to 'accelerator billing' at contracted overage rates but we cap effective billing to 1.25x for the initial acceleration month to avoid runaway charges.

Questions for VectorAI: do you want the frontloaded drawdown for year 1 (helps deploy capacity quickly) or prefer flat monthly drawdown? Frontload helps if you expect short-term spikes and prefer Redwood to reserve capacity.

Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Wang <alex.wang@vectorai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vectorai.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RDW-4521 — draft economics and holdback options

Ben / Grace — quick answers from product + ops:
- Frontloaded drawdown is preferable for us for year 1 (we have a launch window in Q2 where traffic will spike), but we need a hard cap on accelerator step-ups so we don't breach budget. The cap you suggested (1.25x) sounds reasonable as long as true-ups allow cash return if we miss ramp.
- On the refund/holdback split: can we propose 80% cash refund / 20% retained buffer for Option B (24m)? That reduces enterprise finance exposure on slow ramp and still gives Redwood a buffer to cover unanticipated overages.

We will upload the month-by-month ramp profile (conservative / expected / upside) to the Drive link you shared by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product, VectorAI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vectorai.com>, Alex Wang <alex.wang@vectorai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Operational terms — 6-month true-up, reporting & escrow

Lisa/Alex — operationally, here is what we will need to support the holdback + true-up construct:
- Monthly usage reports: Redwood will provide token-level usage export and per-route cost breakdown by the 5th business day of each month. VectorAI must confirm any usage disputes within 10 business days.
- True-up window: every 6 months we compute remaining committed balance. VectorAI can elect (a) cash refund of X% (as negotiated) OR (b) convert refunded amount into an overage buffer at a discounted rate.
- Escrow/holdback mechanism: for medium/large deals we offer escrow of the holdback portion (we can put the retained buffer in a restricted credit account with audit logs accessible to VectorAI). Escrow custody can be sized as a percentage of the committed wallet.
- Early termination: standard clause is pro-rata refund less a termination fee equal to 3 months of committed baseline unless the parties agree alternate terms upfront. For 24-month deals we can negotiate a stepped termination fee schedule.

If VectorAI prefers, we can add a milestone-based release for some of the holdback (e.g., 25% of holdback releases after hitting RU_1: 50% of expected run-rate for two consecutive months).

I'll put a short operational annex into the proposal that maps the true-up calculation and sample worked example. Grace/Ben: want to include this annex with the next proposal iteration.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@vectorai.com>, Alex Wang <alex.wang@vectorai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Final — updated proposal & next steps (RDW-4521)

Lisa / Alex — thanks for the ramp profile and the quick inputs. Attached is an updated proposal and a sample drawdown workbook. Changes from the April 1 draft:
- Option B (24m) updated to an 80/20 refund/retained split at 6-month true-ups (per your ask).
- Frontloaded drawdown preserved for year 1 (first 3 months at 60% baseline), with a capped accelerator of 1.25x per month for initial acceleration months.
- Added milestone release language: 25% of holdback released upon hitting 50% of expected run-rate for two consecutive months.
- Operational annex (Karthik) included: sample true-up math, reporting cadence, and dispute timeline.

Next steps: please confirm (a) preferred option (A or B), (b) acceptance of milestone release, and (c) confirmation you received the Drive upload. Once we have that, Ben will issue an LOI and we can route legal for a short amendment to the MSA.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting you ramped.

Best,
Grace
Director, Enterprise GTM — Redwood Inference
